title: Generic reducedness through strict transform and smooth comparison
statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] which is generically reduced: $\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ is reduced for every generic point $\eta$ of every irreducible component [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components]. Then these local rings are fields, hence regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. If $J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ is a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type with nowhere dense zero set (containing no nonempty open subset), its ordinary blowup $b:X^+=\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)\to X$ is locally Noetherian and generically reduced [pqf-def-coherent, def-nagata-global-blowup]. The open $b^{-1}(X\setminus V(J))$ is dense in every irreducible component of $X^+$; the component generic points correspond bijectively to those of $X$, with identical local rings. For any closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow P$ and a finite-type quasi-coherent ambient center whose extended ideal is $J$, the scheme-theoretic strict transform of $X$ is canonically this same $X^+$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-strict-transform]. No reducedness away from the generic points and no regularity of the center or ambient scheme are required.

If $v:Y\to X$ is any smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], then $Y$ is locally Noetherian and generically reduced, and generic points upstairs map to generic points downstairs. Smooth pullback of a finite ambient blowup/strict-transform diagram agrees with the diagram constructed from the extended ideals, including all scheme structures and all earlier ideal centers; an empty pulled-back center gives the identity stage. The comparisons are the canonical flat-base-change comparisons, commute with further pullback, and retain the earlier ideals even when the intrinsic blowup is an identity. Empty schemes and unit center ideals are allowed.

source.place: Tag 036C, lemma-Rk-local-smooth, k=0; strict transforms: divisors.tex Tag 080E, lemma-strict-transform, and its explicit power-torsion chart formula. Generic-point preservation is the schematic-closure/chart argument recorded in the worker report, not a quoted stronger form of 080E.

proof.text: At a component generic point $\eta$, choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be its minimal prime. The affine identification of stalks gives $\mathcal O_{X,\eta}=A_{\mathfrak p}$. Every element of its maximal ideal is nilpotent by the minimal-prime localization lemma, whose first assertion does not require $A$ reduced. Our hypothesis says this local ring itself is reduced, so its maximal ideal is zero. A nonzero local ring with zero maximal ideal is a field: every nonzero element is outside the maximal ideal and hence a unit. The field-regularity lemma now gives regularity. This argument never assumes that $A$ or $X$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 00EU, lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring, first assertion; Tag 00ES, lemma-irreducible (3)

proof.text: Put $U=X\setminus V(J)$. On a Noetherian affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$, there are finitely many minimal primes. If $V(J)$ contained the component $V(\mathfrak p)$, choose for each other minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ an element $s_{\mathfrak q}\in\mathfrak q\setminus\mathfrak p$. Their product $s$ (the empty product is $1$) satisfies $\varnothing\ne D(s)\subseteq V(\mathfrak p)\subseteq V(J)$, contradicting the empty interior. Thus $U$ contains all component generic points. Blowup properness applies to the given finite-type quasi-coherent ideal; proper means in particular finite type. Consequently the locally-Noetherian ascent lemma shows that $X^+$ is locally Noetherian. No quasi-compactness of $X$ is used.

Use the affine local models in the global blowup construction and the finite chart cover for $I=(f_0,\ldots,f_r)$. On $\operatorname{Spec}C$, $C=A[I/a]$, the extended ideal is $(a)$ and multiplication by $a$ is injective. The minimal-prime avoidance lemma therefore puts every minimal prime of $C$ in $D(a)$. This open is exactly the inverse image of $U$ on the chart, since $IC=(a)$. Hence every component generic point of $X^+$ belongs to $b^{-1}U$: being a generic point can be checked in an open neighbourhood, since all generalizations of a point of an open remain in that open. In particular $b^{-1}U$ meets every component in an open containing its generic point, so it is dense in that component.

The complement theorem identifies $b^{-1}U$ with $U$ as schemes. An open neighbourhood contains every generalization of each of its points; therefore a point in an open subscheme is a component generic point exactly when it is one in the whole scheme. Applying this on both sides, and using Steps 2 and 3, gives a bijection of all component generic points of $X^+$ and $X$. Under the same isomorphism their stalks are identical, since restricting a sheaf to an open neighbourhood does not change its stalk. Step 1 makes these stalks fields. Thus $X^+$ is generically reduced. Finally the ambient closed-immersion strict-transform theorem identifies the scheme-theoretic strict transform with $\operatorname{Bl}_JX$, for the extended ideal $J$ specified in the statement. This identifies the actual schemes, including nilpotents away from the generic points.

Let $v:Y\to X$ be smooth. It is flat and locally of finite presentation. A finite presentation $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by the images of the $t_i$, so $v$ is locally of finite type and $Y$ is locally Noetherian by ascent. Choose affine neighbourhoods $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset Y$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ around a generic point $\xi$ and its image. The affine flatness criterion makes $A\to B$ flat. If the contraction $\mathfrak p$ of the minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ had a strictly smaller prime $\mathfrak p_0$, going down would give $\mathfrak q_0\subseteq\mathfrak q$ contracting to $\mathfrak p_0$. Minimality forces $\mathfrak q_0=\mathfrak q$, a contradiction. Thus $v(\xi)$ is a component generic point of $X$.

source.place: Tag 00HS, lemma-flat-going-down; descent.tex Tag 036C, lemma-Rk-local-smooth, k=0

proof.text: For $\xi$ as in Step 5, put $\eta=v(\xi)$. Step 1 says $\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ is a field and its maximal ideal is zero. Smoothness gives a geometrically reduced fibre $Y_\eta$, hence a reduced local ring $\mathcal O_{Y_\eta,\xi}$. The fibre-stalk quotient isomorphism identifies this ring with $\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}/\mathfrak m_\eta\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}=\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}$. This proves generic reducedness of $Y$. Also $v^{-1}U$ contains every component generic point of $Y$, since its image is a component generic point in $U$. Thus extended nowhere dense centres remain nowhere dense. This uses neither surjectivity nor reducedness of $X$ away from its generic points.

source.place: Tag 0HA1, lemma-local-ring-fibre; varieties.tex Tag 056T, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal; descent.tex Tag 036C, lemma-Rk-local-smooth

proof.text: For an ambient diagram $X\hookrightarrow P$ and a smooth cartesian pullback $P_1\to P$, the induced map $Y=X\times_PP_1\to X$ is smooth. Indeed relative dimension is locally constant for a smooth map, so around any point one restricts to relative dimension $n$ and applies the relative-dimension permanence lemma; smoothness is local by its definition. Use smooth-flatness, the flat blowup comparison, and the scheme strict-transform flat-base-change theorem. Its extra generic-point hypothesis on $Y\to X$ is exactly Step 5. It identifies the pulled-back closed strict transform, with its scheme structure and its map into the ambient blowup, with the strict transform of $Y$ for the extended ambient ideal. For intrinsic blowups, the flat blowup comparison applies directly to any smooth $Y\to X$. On affine charts these are the specified maps $B\otimes_A A[I/a]\xrightarrow{\sim}B[IB/\varphi(a)]$, $b\otimes(c/a)\mapsto b\varphi(c)/\varphi(a)$, including the structural maps and the centre ideals. The cited chart-restriction theorem also identifies the overlap localizations. Thus these are precisely the canonical flat-base-change comparisons.

source.place: Tag 0805, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up; morphisms.tex Tag 081I, lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image; Tag 01VB, lemma-base-change-smooth

proof.text: For a further pullback with coefficient maps $A\xrightarrow{\varphi}B\xrightarrow{\psi}C$, both chart comparisons send $d\otimes(b\otimes(c/a))$ to $d\psi(b)\psi\varphi(c)/\psi\varphi(a)$. They therefore agree: these tensors and fractions generate the chart algebras, and the overlap maps are the corresponding localizations. For any earlier ideal $K=(k_\lambda)$ its successive extensions have generators $\psi\varphi(k_\lambda)$, exactly the generators of its extension along the composite. This also describes the scheme-theoretic inverse-image centre by the ideal-image formula. Starting with the identity comparison at stage zero, apply Step 7 at each next blowup and strict transform; the comparison at that stage preserves all earlier extended ideals by this generator calculation. The new vertical maps are base changes of the original smooth map, hence smooth by the same local constant-relative-dimension argument as in Step 7. This induction proves the assertion for every finite diagram, and the displayed equality proves compatibility with further pullback.

source.place: Tag 0805, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up, coefficientwise comparison; schemes.tex Tag 01JU, lemma-fibre-product-immersion (1)

proof.text: If a pulled-back centre is empty, its ideal is the unit ideal. The complement is then the whole scheme and the complement isomorphism gives the identity blowup stage. Any earlier ideal is still extended along this isomorphism: it is not replaced by the unit ideal merely because the current blowup is an identity. The same bookkeeping applies when a non-unit centre happens to have identity blowup. Unit ideals thus cause no exception in the induction; on the empty scheme all generic-point assertions are vacuous and all comparisons are the unique corresponding maps. None of Steps 1--8 requires a regular centre or regular ambient scheme.

lean.statement: theorem genericallyReduced_blowup_geometry (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents X, ∀ η : X, IsGenericPoint η C → _root_.IsReduced (X.presheaf.stalk η)) : (∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents X, ∀ η : X, IsGenericPoint η C → IsField (X.presheaf.stalk η) ∧ IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk η)) ∧ (∀ (J : X.IdealSheafData), J.ofFiniteType → interior (J.support : Set X) = ∅ → IsLocallyNoetherian J.blowup ∧ (∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents J.blowup, ∀ ξ : J.blowup, IsGenericPoint ξ C → _root_.IsReduced (J.blowup.presheaf.stalk ξ)) ∧ (∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents J.blowup, Dense ((Subtype.val : C → J.blowup) ⁻¹' (J.blowupMap ⁻¹' (J.support.compl : Set X)))) ∧ (∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents J.blowup, ∀ ξ : J.blowup, IsGenericPoint ξ C → J.blowupMap ξ ∈ J.support.compl ∧ (∃ D ∈ irreducibleComponents X, IsGenericPoint (J.blowupMap ξ) D) ∧ IsIso (J.blowupMap.stalkMap ξ)) ∧ (∀ D ∈ irreducibleComponents X, ∀ η : X, IsGenericPoint η D → ∃! ξ : J.blowup, J.blowupMap ξ = η ∧ ∃ C ∈ irreducibleComponents J.blowup, IsGenericPoint ξ C) ∧ (∀ (P : Scheme.{u}) (i : X ⟶ P) [IsClosedImmersion i] (I : P.IdealSheafData), I.ofFiniteType → I.comap i = J → ∃ e : J.blowup ≅ I.strictTransform i, e.hom ≫ strictTransformToSource i I.blowupMap I.support.compl = J.blowupMap ∧ (e.hom ≫ strictTransformMap i I.blowupMap I.support.compl) ≫ I.blowupMap = J.blowupMap ≫ i))
